claims.claim_text: Because a checkpoint can only reset the WAL when no other connection is using it, a checkpoint will always reset the WAL whenever the WAL is unused.

A PASSIVE checkpoint might not reset even if unused if it hasn't reached the end of the WAL content to transfer, though typically it tries to complete. However, the text emphasizes that PASSIVE checkpoints 'might not run to completion'. The logical leap from 'can only reset if unused' to 'will always reset if unused' ignores the behavior of PASSIVE checkpoints which may stop early for other reasons or simply not be invoked.
